cover.headline: Blockbuster could have bought Netflix. {It passed.}
cover.credit: Photo: Phillip Pessar / CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons

slides.label: THE EMPIRE
slides.headline: About {9,000 stores.}
slides.body: At its peak, *Blockbuster* ran roughly *9,000 stores.* Friday night meant walking down an aisle of cassettes and DVDs. Netflix was a young *DVD-by-mail* company.

slides.label: THE MONEY MACHINE
slides.headline: {$800 million} in late fees.
slides.body: In *2000,* Blockbuster collected about *$800 million* in late fees, roughly *16% of its revenue,* AP reported. Customers hated them. Netflix's subscription had *no late fees.*
slides.source: AP via Mental Floss; Business Insider

slides.label: THE OFFER
slides.headline: A {$50 million} offer.
slides.body: Netflix's co-founders say they offered to *sell to Blockbuster* for *$50 million.* Reed Hastings' book says CEO John Antioco *declined.* Antioco has disputed that any serious talks took place.

slides.label: THE FALL
slides.headline: {Bankrupt} in 2010.
slides.body: Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy in *September 2010* to wipe out around *$1 billion* of debt. Its late-fee U-turn had reportedly cost an estimated *$200 million.*

slides.label: THE FLIP
slides.headline: Netflix: {300 million+} members.
slides.body: By the end of *2024,* Netflix reported over *300 million* paid memberships. Hastings has said: *"Thank God"* Blockbuster didn't take the deal.

last.headline: Your biggest profit can be {your customers' biggest complaint.}
last.body: Late fees were 16% of Blockbuster's revenue, and Netflix built a business on removing them. Would you have bought Netflix for $50 million?
